title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity as commercial partnerships expand and defense budgets grow. Meanwhile, the specter of space weather looms over technology advancements, and hypersonic tests continue to face delays.

themes.title: Commercial Space Station Partnerships
themes.body: Vast's recent partnerships for microgravity research underscore the growing interest in commercial space stations. As private entities step up, the dynamics of space research are shifting away from traditional government-led initiatives.

themes.title: Defense Spending on the Rise
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adds a significant $1.4 billion to space resilience efforts, highlighting the increasing prioritization of space in national defense. This trend suggests a long-term commitment to bolstering capabilities against emerging threats.

themes.title: Hypersonic Testing Woes
themes.body: The latest hypersonic glide-vehicle test has slipped yet again, marking the third consecutive quarter of delays. This raises questions about the feasibility and reliability of hypersonic technology in the near term.

themes.title: AI's Space Weather Dilemma
themes.body: As AI technologies proliferate, concerns about space weather's impact on their performance are surfacing. This intersection of space and AI could complicate future advancements, especially in critical defense applications.
